features.title: agent-comms — Handoff Contract v1
features.tldr: handoff-v1.2 separates HTML reports from JSON handoffs and carries the self_pull Layer-1 read-proof line.
features.summary: the handoff-v1 family contract separates human evidence from agent-to-agent coordination: HTML reports in .dadaia/reports/<context>/<agent>/ and JSON handoffs in .dadaia/handoff/<context>/. Current version handoff-v1.2 requires self_pull.refs — the Layer-1 memory atoms the session actually read (specs/-prefixed, existence-checked, role-map coverage) — with historical v1/v1.1 documents valid forever (transition posture). The CLI validates schema, the v1.2 self_pull conditional, and artifact.path hash inside the workspace — any existing relative path under the root resolves workspace-rooted (incl. repos/<slug>/specs/audits), with a legacy handoff-dir fallback; reports next and the QA/security gate consume the canonical root.

features.title: agent-monitoring
features.tldr: stdlib-only local telemetry (Claude/Codex/PI sessions) → panel Sessions tab + /api/agents; allowlist gate preserves privacy.
features.summary: stdlib-only local telemetry consuming Claude Code jsonl + Codex sqlite (~/.codex/state_5.sqlite) + PI session jsonl (~/.pi/agent/sessions/); feeds the panel's Sessions tab and the /api/agents and /api/sessions endpoints; a hardcoded allowlist gate preserves privacy by construction; endpoints served with no credential behind the panel's loopback bind + Host allowlist.

features.title: agent-orchestration
features.tldr: Nine core Layer-1 roles, eight Layer-2 personas, two dispatchers, four workflows, and advisory-only concurrency.
features.summary: Defines role ownership, dispatch purity, memory bootstrap, task discipline, review checkpoints, model governance, and the relationship between Layer-1 agents and Layer-2 workflow personas. No role acquires or coordinates a concurrency lock.

features.title: academy
features.tldr: browsable knowledge_basis in the panel's Academy tab + copy-from-template management via CLI.
features.summary: the panel's Academy tab browses the knowledge_basis modules directly (GET /api/academy lists all modules with titles and lesson counts; the read-only traversal-guarded route GET /academy/<module>/<lesson> renders the lesson in Markdown). The copy-from-template CLI (dadaia academy create/update/delete) remains the management surface for derived courses.

features.title: plugin-packs
features.tldr: in-package plugin packs (4 skills each) enabled via `dadaia plugin install`, disabled via `uninstall`; 3 stub agents gain real behavior once installed.
features.summary: The plugin-distribution capability — in-package packs under public/plugins/ (frontend-design + devops, 4 skills each), the `dadaia plugin install/uninstall/list/doctor` CLI on a ports-and-adapters seam (PluginPack/InstalledPlugins core model + PluginStore port + JsonPluginStore adapter), a per-workspace installed_plugins.json ledger, profile-scoped projection that overwrites the projected core stub with the pack's real agent body, core-install precedence so a later public install never reverts an installed pack, an uninstall inverse (files-first/ledger-last, never-silent drift restore, never-installed equivalence), plugin doctor per-file status, machine-checked pack-agent skill refs, and the three plugin agents (frontend-engineer, design-specialist, devops-engineer) carrying real behavior on the registry plugin/sonnet tier once their pack is installed.

features.title: public-asset-distribution
features.tldr: canonical public assets are staged to .dadaia/agentic and projected to Claude Code, Codex, PI, and shared .agents roots.
features.summary: Describes the canonical public asset chain, hash-compare install overwrite, staging-vs-projected drift detection, privacy gate, harness-profile-aware install/doctor, render-at-install of core agents (staged generic body + resolved agent-model policy composed into both L1 projections) with a policy-aware doctor render-compare, plugin-pack projection with installed-plugins ledger + core-install precedence + uninstall reconciliation (files-first/ledger-last inverse), provenance-gated consumer AGENTS fan-out (banner-canonical restored vs hand-authored left [foreign]) with lexical repo-slug containment + destination-file symlink refusal, scoped AGENTS projections, source-root hygiene guard, and runtime projection contract.

features.title: pypi-distribution
features.tldr: The published dadaia-workspace 0.2.x PyPI package, the release.yml OIDC publish pipeline, the wheel content contract, and the SDD-vs-package version split.
features.summary: Owns PyPI distribution as product behavior — the live `dadaia-workspace` 0.2.x package (PyPI since PRs #112/#113, ratified v0.1.61), the `.github/workflows/release.yml` pipeline (version-vs-tag check → five test legs → build → release-gate approval → OIDC trusted publishing + tag → post-publish smoke), the wheel content contract (plugin packs and public assets ship in-package), and the documented version-scheme split: SDD releases `v0.1.x` version the SDD process while the package `0.2.x` versions the shipped library (ADR-2 — documented, never renumbered).

features.title: Harness — Claude Code
features.tldr: Layer-1-only entry harness; richest deterministic enforcement; scaffold = CLAUDE.md bridge + .claude/ projection (agents, skills, rules, hooks).
features.summary: Capability and scaffold truth for the Claude Code harness — what it can do at each agentic layer, what dadaia projects for it, its enforcement posture, and what a Claude-only workspace installation contains.

features.title: Harness — Codex
features.tldr: Dual-layer Codex harness with projected hooks in TUI and headless exec, a governed CODEX_EXEC worker, and independent git chokepoints.
features.summary: Capability and scaffold truth for the Codex harness at both agentic layers — shared hook enforcement, the CODEX_EXEC worker transport, model catalog, and what a Codex-only workspace installation contains.

features.title: Harness - PI (pi-coding-agent)
features.tldr: Dual-layer PI runtime with a trusted TypeScript entry extension and a governed headless worker supporting Codex-subscription and explicit OpenRouter profiles.
features.summary: PI can enter the workspace interactively after explicit trust and can execute bounded Layer-2 workflow steps through `pi --mode json`. GPT profiles use provider-qualified Codex-subscription ids; optional OpenRouter profiles remain explicit.

features.title: brand-identity
features.tldr: canonical 5-color palette and CSS tokens of the panel (release dadaia-workspace-brand-identity-v1).
features.summary: canonical 5-color palette and CSS tokens of the panel (release dadaia-workspace-brand-identity-v1).

features.title: panel
features.tldr: Loopback-only local control surface with seven tabs, four workflow diagrams/policies, agent governance, telemetry, reports, and playable Snake/Tetris.
features.summary: `dadaia panel` serves the local workspace UI. Its seven tabs are Projects, 1st Agentic Layer, 2nd Agentic Layer, Reports, Academy, Servers, and Games. It is loopback-only, no-auth, Host-guarded, and CSP-constrained.

features.title: product-vision
features.tldr: A strict, portable SDD workspace that gives agents current context, four reliable workflows, visible concurrency, and strong anti-slop boundaries.
features.summary: Defines dadaia-workspace as a local-first environment for context-bound agent work. It combines canonical specs and memory, deterministic safety gates, four executable lifecycle workflows, cross-harness projections, auditable evidence, and explicit workspace/repository hygiene.

features.title: spec-context-project
features.tldr: One canonical specs tree plus one repository, explicitly bindable by each session and safe for visible concurrent work.
features.summary: The central unit of dadaia-workspace. Binding selects the project and injects its current memory for the caller; the SDD gate and workflows constrain writes while advisory presence surfaces concurrent sessions without locking them out.

features.title: context-management
features.tldr: ALIVE/DEAD context registry, caller-owned session binding, bind-driven memory injection, and advisory presence with no concurrency locks.
features.summary: Manages Spec Context Projects and their repositories. Bind persists context and mode only for the caller, writes the bind-epoch injection marker, and never acquires a lock. Concurrent work is allowed and surfaced through expiring presence records.

features.title: cross-platform-portability
features.tldr: Linux, macOS, and Windows support through a single platform capability seam, injected adapters, Python hooks, and hard-gated cross-OS tests.
features.summary: `core/platform.py` owns platform detection. OS-sensitive behavior is behind ports and infrastructure adapters; security failures are loud, non-security features degrade explicitly, and unsupported capabilities fail at construction.

features.title: multi-platform-parity
features.tldr: Claude Code, Codex, and PI receive truthful runtime-specific projections from one canonical public source.
features.summary: Defines Layer-1 projection parity without pretending the harnesses have identical primitives. Codex and PI also provide Layer-2 workflow workers; Claude remains Layer-1-only. Git chokepoints protect commit/push independently of harness hooks.

features.title: repos-catalog
features.tldr: repos.xlsx lookup for fast discovery of known repos with slug + URL.
features.summary: repos.xlsx lookup for fast discovery of known repos with slug + URL.

features.title: server-registry
features.tldr: internal port registry with TTL+PID to avoid conflicts between parallel agents' dev servers; the 3000-3999 range applies only to next_port allocation.
features.summary: internal port registry with TTL+PID to avoid conflicts between parallel agents' dev servers. The 3000-3999 range is enforced only by next_port allocation; register() accepts any port.

features.title: workspace-doctor
features.tldr: Diagnoses root hygiene, venv health, context coherence, stale presence, and retired lock-state residue; repairs only deterministic state.
features.summary: `dadaia doctor` checks workspace-root law, forbidden caches, required state layout, workspace venv health, context repository coherence, repo URLs, stale presence, and legacy lock/pointer residue. `--fix` performs bounded deterministic cleanup.

features.title: workspace-init
features.tldr: Idempotent bootstrap of workspace state, Python venv, selected harness projections, and governance hooks.
features.summary: `dadaia init` creates the canonical `.dadaia/` runtime, provisions `.dadaia/.venv`, records the harness profile, stages/installs public assets, and configures runtime hooks without creating repository-local state.

features.title: workspace-portability
features.tldr: export/import of the whole workspace as a tar.gz for backup or migration between machines.
features.summary: export/import of the whole workspace as a tar.gz for backup or migration between machines.

features.title: dadaia-workflows
features.tldr: Exactly four executable Layer-2 workflows: backlog definition, release definition, implementation plus reviews, and audit.
features.summary: The complete executable workflow surface. Each workflow has one CLI command, a Python-owned ordered body, fragment-plus-persona worker prompts, semantic gates, immutable per-attempt payloads, and an auditable handoff graph. Codex and PI are the supported real Layer-2 workers; fake is the deterministic test adapter.

features.title: lifecycle-foundation
features.tldr: Deterministic Python workflow engine with fragment-scoped workers, semantic gates, bounded retries, and immutable handoff evidence.
features.summary: The runtime foundation beneath the four dadaia-workflows. Python owns sequencing, context selection, policy resolution, task-marker and artifact gates, run state, retries, diagnostics, and retention. Codex and PI workers run behind AgentRuntimePort.

features.title: sdd-bug-backlog-governance
features.tldr: Event-sourced JSONL bugs, duplicate-safe backlog definition, release consumption, audit dispositions, and exact-commit security-gated push.
features.summary: Bugs are append-only events; backlog definition binds canonical subjects and prevents duplicate/conflicting intake; release definition consumes explicit items; closure and audit require terminal dispositions. Intake is additive and never lock-gated.

features.title: sdd-gate-v3
features.tldr: No-lock SDD enforcement: deterministic path/mode gates, advisory presence, warn-only concurrent commits, and a security-gated push boundary.
features.summary: The merged Python PreToolUse gate enforces root whitelist, workspace venv usage, path class, phase, and the caller's own mode. It never waits for or blocks on another session. Presence is advisory. Git pre-commit warns only; pre-push enforces CI and an approved security handoff for every pushed commit.

features.title: specs-doctor
features.tldr: Validates canonical specs structure, memory/catalog integrity, release markers, closure evidence, dispositions, bug ledgers, and audit coherence.
features.summary: `dadaia specs doctor` coordinates structural, memory, release, closure/audit, governance, and coherence validators. `--fix` performs only deterministic repairs.
